subject: Does variable type matter in input table for modelling?

messages.author: 77e0f8e9f257430f
messages.subject: Does variable type matter in input table for modelling?
parts:
Hello! I’m currently trying to fit some detectability models and these are the covariates and factors I want to test:


Day (1,2,3, and so on)
Observer (Bogdan and Adam)
Rain (0 or 1)
Wind (Beaufort scale, 0-5)
Cloud (0-4)


My question is what kind of variables I should tell R that they are. “Observer” is obviously a factor, but when it comes to day, rain, wind and cloud, the str() tells me that they are read as integers. This is true, since they can’t have decimal values. But should I convert them to factors before I start to fit the models (because of the fixed scale values)? Or does it not matter? I have tried fitting models without changing anything and it works, but I’m not sure how R interprets them in the unmarkedFrameOccu() function. And if I do need to change them into factors, how do I do that?


This is my code:


test_occu <- read.csv("C:/Users/PC/Documents/Examensarbete/Data/HOM_redbackedshrike.csv", dec=".", sep=”;”)


y <- test_occu[,2:3] #The frequencies for 1st survey and 2nd survey

siteCovs <- test_occu[,4:11] #The habitat data (occupancy cov)

obsCovs <- list(Day=test_occu[,c("Day1", "Day2")],

                Observer=test_occu[,c("Observer1", "Observer2")],

                Rain=test_occu[,c("Rain1", "Rain2")],

                Wind=test_occu[,c("Wind1", "Wind2")],

                Cloud=test_occu[,c("Cloud1", "Cloud2")]) #The weather, etc. (detection cov)


str(obsCovs) #Output says that they are interpreted as integers


#Create the unmarkedFrameOccu()

umf <- unmarkedFrameOccu(y, siteCovs=siteCovs, obsCovs=obsCovs)


#Fit detection models####

dm1 <- occu(~ 1 ~ 1, umf) #Null model
dm2 <- occu(~ Wind ~ 1, umf)
dm3 <- occu(~ Cloud ~ 1, umf)
dm4 <- occu(~ Day ~ 1, umf)
dm5 <- occu(~ Wind + Cloud ~ 1, umf)
dm6 <- occu(~ Day + Wind ~ 1, umf)
dm7 <- occu(~ Day + Cloud ~ 1, umf)
dm8 <- occu(~ Day + Wind + Cloud ~ 1, umf)


#Compare detectability models

dms <- fitList('psi(.)p(.)' = dm1, #Null model

               'psi(.)p(Wind)' = dm2,

               'psi(.)p(Cloud)' = dm3,

               'psi(.)p(Day)' = dm4,

               'psi(.)p(Wind+Cloud)' = dm5,

               'psi(.)p(Day+Wind)' = dm6,

               'psi(.)p(Day+Cloud)' = dm7,

               'psi(.)p(Day+Wind+Cloud)' = dm8)


#Select the best detectability model (should have delta AIC<2)
#If the null model is included in best model set, then no covariates are good

modSel(dms)


Thanks in advance!
